item.text: {"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"During 2023, several central and local measures became observable administrative practice rather than remaining only plans. Fiscal authorities reported executed tax reductions, transfers, social-assistance funding, infrastructure and disaster-recovery spending; national medical-insurance administration reported coverage, inspections, sanctions, fund recovery, medical assistance, and treatment use; and a county administration documented actual subsistence payments, elderly services, temporary assistance, and related local programs (BATCH-0007-E001; BATCH-0016-E009; BATCH-0020-E002). Budget-management and debt directives also produced monitoring systems, inspections, public accountability cases, budget integration, and enforcement actions, although the same official account acknowledged continuing irregular borrowing, inefficient fund use, and incomplete local implementation (BATCH-0007-E006; BATCH-0003-E010). Enforcement practice is also observable in cyberspace policing and content controls, including investigations, platform actions, account closures, and content removals, though official classifications and their broader policy value are not independently established (BATCH-0002-E003; BATCH-0001-E009; BATCH-0010-E001). Military-governance directives and a revised conscription regulation were formally issued or put into force, but the supplied account does not independently verify compliance or operational results (BATCH-0019-E011). The record is therefore mixed: implementation was substantial in fiscal administration, health-insurance administration, social assistance, and selected enforcement systems, but legislation or directives scheduled for future effect—including the revised Administrative Reconsideration Law and the Online Protection Regulation—cannot establish 2023 implementation, while some enacted protections had weak or uncertain enforcement (BATCH-0019-E002; BATCH-0021-E003; BATCH-0010-E025; BATCH-0001-E011). These records show state-system practice during Xi’s 2023 tenure, but generally do not prove Xi’s personal authorship or causal responsibility for each measure, nor do they establish completion, quality, or success across the broader governing
